build.title: Reading Log
build.brief:
Build a small two-screen "Reading Log" web app for personal use.
- Screen 1, Log: a list of books (title, author, status: reading / finished, date finished), newest first, with a filter (all / reading / finished) and an empty state.
- Screen 2, Add/Edit: a form (title required, author, status, date finished shown only when finished) with Save, Cancel and Delete (edit only, with a confirm step).
- Data stays in the browser (localStorage). Plain static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no external requests or fonts; mobile-first, works at 360 px wide, accessible (labels, focus states, contrast).
- Keep the plan small: two screens, then ship. This is the first real run of the team loop.

styles.css: the error rule is `.field .err`, but the new save and delete messages are `

` inside `#save-err` (a direct child of .form) and `#delete-err` (inside .confirm), not inside `.field`, so they render as plain unstyled text. They must be red (var(--danger)), 14px/600, per item 2. Also check `.confirm p { margin: 0 0 var(--s3); }` doesn't override the delete message's margin or colour (.confirm .err wins if you add it). Nothing else changes.

Round 2. The fix is live in ~/work/app/ (no git; writing there is the deploy).
1. Done: store.js add/update now return null when the write fails, and remove returns false. edit.js checks the result and navigates to the Log only after a confirmed write. On failure the form, entered data or the delete confirm stays as it was. Cases that got no event handling beyond this: the Log is unchanged.
2. Done: edit.html has a `role="alert"` region just above Save/Cancel, and one inside the confirm panel. Failures fill it with a red `.err` message using the exact copy: "Couldn't save. Your browser storage may be full. Your changes are still on this page." and "Couldn't delete this book. Your browser storage may be unavailable." The save message clears on the next edit or attempt. The delete message clears on retry or Keep book/Escape. styles.css has two small rules so the empty regions take no space.
3. Not done: I did not re-run any tests, so I have no fault-test or browser results to report. I have no browser here, so I can't simulate a quota error. I only re-read the code. Max has said they will rerun the real browser fault test, and normal add/edit/delete/filter/reload needs a browser run too.
Changed files: store.js, edit.js, edit.html, styles.css. Nothing else changed.
